Lemma
[Laplace-method asymptotics for a ratio of Gaussian-type integrals] 1. ch4:4.5.2-lem-1\group Asymptotics If continuous $k,l:\R \to \R $ have $k$ growing at least quadratically, $l$ at most linearly, and $k$ has a unique minimizer $y_0$, then \[ \lim _{\varepsilon \to 0} \frac{\int _\R l(y)e^{-k(y)/\varepsilon }\, dy}{\int _\R e^{-k(y)/\varepsilon }\, dy}=l(y_0). \]

Proof

\sketch Normalize $e^{-(k-k(y_0))/\varepsilon }$ to a probability density. Quadratic growth gives domination and concentration at the unique minimizer; the weighted averages of the at-most-linear function $l$ therefore converge to $l(y_0)$.

□
